why: A direct mattress seller with $16-45 million of sales per area and advertising of $1.2-5.4 million (about 4-14% of sales) is believable.
An agency with $81 million revenue across twelve accounts and 300 staff gives about $270,000 per head, with accounts ranging from about $100,000 to $460,000 per head, which is believable.
Car insurance branches writing $25-62 million of premiums at running costs of $0.9-4.7 million (roughly 2-11% of premiums) are believable.
All four pies sum to 100%, and 1,300 respondents being 26% of a district base of about 5,000 small-business clients is believable for a broker.
Multiplexes drawing 550-2,300 visitors a day with queues of 5-12 minutes, and a $2 million site earning $1.50 per visitor (about $600,000 a year), are believable for developing markets.
Subcontractor and repair costs sit within each line's total, and 184 repairs costing $37,500 (about $200, or 8 carpenter hours at $26, each) with wages of $18-26 an hour is believable.
Household incomes of about $2,000-10,400 at market rates, with PPP rates below market rates, fit emerging economies.
Language schools earning $6-21 million in fees with promotion budgets of $0.6-2.4 million (about 7-19% of fees) are large but within a few times of a real chain's schools.

A packaging supplier with about 17% of $3-3.6 billion segment markets and $3.5-6.5 million of revenue per sales rep is believable, and in the latest year films revenue grows more slowly than its market, as the CEO's concern says.
Twelve studios with $77 million revenue and 350 architects give about $220,000 per architect, between $100,000 and $330,000 by studio, which is believable for an architecture practice.
